---
title: "cf Build Output module discovery"
description: "How wave-1 cf Build Output emits choose Worker modules, and why Vite RSC graphs need import-following."
---

`discoverCfBuildOutputEsmModules` (in `scripts/ci/cf-build-output-publisher.mjs`)
starts from the `dist/server/.vite/manifest.json` graph. That manifest belongs to
the ssr environment only. A Vite RSC Worker reaches its second environment with
`import.meta.viteRsc.loadModule`, which compiles to
`` import(`./rsc/bridge-api.js`) ``. The `rsc/` graph and
`__vite_rsc_assets_manifest.js` are absent from that manifest. A manifest-only
emit therefore uploads a Worker that starts cleanly, then rejects that import on
every request that reaches it. Finance `831c6aae6f` shipped 222 of 470 modules this
way, and every route returned 500 from the outer response-policy catch.
`wrangler --no-bundle` uploads every module that matches its rules, so it was
unaffected.

The publisher now follows relative static and dynamic specifiers from every
included module, including constant template literals, to files that exist. The
walk is transitive, bounded, stays inside the bundle root and skips dot
directories. Comments inside `import(` are allowed. Non-constant templates such
as `` import(`./rsc/${name}.js`) `` are not followed, so they would need the
manifest or a rules-glob emit. Unimported files stay excluded. `assertModuleClosure` fails emission
when an included module imports an existing module that is outside the upload
set; on the Vite path the walk already adds those, so the assertion is the
backstop for the rules-glob path. `wave1-cf-output` logs the emitted count
against the sealed count. `assertUploadedModuleSet` compares a published
version's module names with the emitted manifest; no publish path calls it yet,
because wiring it needs a names-only read of the published version that stays
within the 1 MiB control-plane response cap. Regression coverage is in
`scripts/ci/cf-build-output-publisher.test.mjs` (RSC layout, a manifest-only
negative control, and the root and dot-directory bounds).

Two cautions apply when you audit a hosted version:

- `GET /workers/scripts/<name>/content/v2` ignores `?version=` and returns the
  latest upload. Do not use it to compare versions.
- `GET /workers/workers/<name>/versions/<id>?include=modules` returns that
  version's module names and bytes, so you can check import closure against the
  version that actually serves traffic.
